posts.headline: Nvidia's revenue doubled last quarter to $115.8 billion — and it's the single biggest stock in most Americans' 401(k).
posts.source: Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 release (SEC), Nov. 17, 2026
posts.caption:
Nvidia just doubled its revenue in three months — and it's probably the biggest bet in your 401(k).

The chipmaker reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the quarter ended Oct. 25, up 103% from a year ago (NVIDIA's SEC filing). Net income: $65.3 billion. Data-center sales jumped 110%.

Why it matters even if you never bought the stock: Nvidia is the world's most valuable company and about 8% of the S&P 500 — the largest single holding in most index funds and 401(k)s.

It's also the first report since founder Jensen Huang stepped down; former CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Shares rose after hours.

My take: one company now moves the fund millions retire on — a lot of eggs in one basket, however good the quarter.

Is Nvidia your biggest holding without you choosing it?
